chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir, from Abu Hamza, or from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, in Al-Kufa there are accursed mosques and blessed mosques. As for the blessed one, it is the Mosque of Ghaniyyin. By Allah, its Qiblah is balanced and just, and its clay is good. A believing man established it, and the world will not pass away until two springs gush out from it and two gardens are in its presence. However, its people are accursed and it is taken away from them. And the Mosque of Bani Zafar, which is the Mosque of Al-Sahla, and a mosque in Al-Khmar'a, and the Mosque of Ju'fi, and it is not their mosque today. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is extinct'.

As for the accursed mosques, they are the Mosque of Thaqif, the Mosque of Al-Ash'ath, the Mosque of Jarir, the Mosque of Simak, and a mosque in Al-Khmar'a built upon the grave of a Pharaoh from the Pharaohs.
ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the accursed and blessed mosques in Al-Kufa according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) distinguishes between mosques in Kufa based on the spiritual integrity of their founders and their physical foundations, highlighting Masjid Ghaniyyin as a blessed site with eschatological signs despite the accursed status of its inhabitants. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the interplay between physical sanctity (such as the quality of clay and direction of Qiblah) and the moral state of the community, contrasting the 'blessed' mosques with those of prominent figures like Al-Ash'ath and Thaqif, which are deemed accursed due to their association with injustice or built upon graves. The mention of springs and gardens emerging reflects the Shia belief in the manifestation of divine blessings in specific holy sites during the end times.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Amro Bin Usman, from Muhammad Bin Uzafir, from Abu Hamza, or from Muhammad Bin Muslim,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘In Al-Kufa there are accursed Masjids and Blessed Masjids. So, as for the Blessed, so it is Masjid Ghaniyyin. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Its (direction of) Qiblah is balanced and just and as its clay (is good), and a Believing man has established (founded) it, and before the end of world two fountains will gush out from it and two gardens happen to be in its presence. However, the people around it are condemned and the Masjid is taken away from them. And the Masjid of the Clan of Zafar (is another such) Masjid, And another Masjid is in Al-Khamra’a, and Masjid Ju’fy, and it is not their Masjid today’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is extinct’.
So, as for the accursed Masjids, so it is Masjid Saqeef, and Masjid Al-Ash’as, and Masjid Jareer, and Masjid Simak, and Masjid at Al-Khamra’a built upon a grave of a Pharaoh from the Pharohs’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman from Muhammad ibn ‘ Adhafir from abu Hamzah or from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“In Kufa there are condemned Masjids and blessed Masjids. One of the blessed Masjids is the Masjid of Ghany. By Allah, the direction of Qiblah thereof is balanced and just and its soil is blessed. A believing man established it and before the end of the world, two fountains will gush forth there-from with two gardens nearby. However, the people around it are condemned and the Masjid is taken away from them. Banu Zafar’s, al-Sahlah Masjid, is another such Masjid. Another Masjid is in al-Khumrah and yet another one is Al-Ju‘fiy Masjid and today it is not their Masjid. He said, ‘It is destroyed.’
“Other condemned Masjid are Saqif, al-Ash‘ath and Jarir Masjids. There is also Sammak Masjid in al-Khumrah which is built on the grave of a pharaoh of the pharaohs.”
